facts.statement: The genus Dorygnathus was formally named by Johann Andreas Wagner in 1860.
facts.quote: authority: Wagner, 1860

facts.statement: Dorygnathus lived during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Jurassic,

facts.statement: The holotype of Dorygnathus is a lower jaw specimen designated PSB 757.
facts.quote: The holotype, a lower jaw, is specimen PSB 757.

facts.statement: A Dorygnathus specimen was discovered in Nancy, France, in 1978.
facts.quote: One specimen, SMNS 81840, has in 1978 been dug up in Nancy, France.

facts.statement: Most Dorygnathus fossils were found in two major waves of discovery during the 1920s and the 1980s.
facts.quote: Most fossils were found in two major waves, one during the 1920s, the other during the 1980s.

facts.statement: Rupert Wild described and named the species Dorygnathus mistelgauensis in 1971.
facts.quote: In 1971 Rupert Wild described and named a second species: Dorygnathus mistelgauensis

facts.statement: Dorygnathus had a short wingspan of approximately 1.5 meters.
facts.quote: It had a short wingspan around 1.5 m

facts.statement: Dorygnathus had a long skull with eye sockets that were the largest openings in the skull.
facts.quote: Its skull was long and its eye sockets were the largest opening therein.

facts.statement: Dorygnathus possessed large curved fangs at the front of its snout and smaller straighter teeth along the back.
facts.quote: Large curved fangs that "intermeshed" when the jaws closed featured prominently at the front of the snout while smaller, straighter teeth lined the back.

facts.statement: Evidence from gut contents suggests that Dorygnathus was a piscivore, or fish-eater.
facts.quote: Its heterodont dentition and direct dietary evidence based on gut contents suggest that Dorygnathus is a piscivore (fish-eater).

facts.statement: The largest known skull of Dorygnathus measures sixteen centimetres in length.
facts.quote: The largest known cranium, that of specimen MBR 1920.16 prepared by Bernard Hauff in 1915 and eventually acquired by the Natural History Museum of Berlin, has a length of sixteen centimetres.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of the largest known specimen is 147 millimetres long.
facts.quote: In MBR 1920.16, the mandibula as a whole has a length of 147 millimetres.

facts.statement: Dorygnathus possessed at least 44 teeth in its jaws.
facts.quote: The total number of teeth is thus at least 44.

facts.statement: The lower arm of Dorygnathus is 60% longer than its upper arm.
facts.quote: The lower arm is 60% longer than the upper arm.

facts.statement: Dorygnathus lived in Europe approximately 180 million years ago during the Early Jurassic when shallow seas covered much of the continent.
facts.quote: Dorygnathus («mandíbula de lanza») es un género extinto de pterosaurio que vivió en Europa a principios del período Jurásico, hace 180 millones de años cuando los mares poco profundos inundaron la mayor parte del continente.

facts.statement: Dorygnathus had a wingspan of 1.5 metres.
facts.quote: Tenía una corta envergadura de 1.5metros

facts.statement: Dorygnathus is commonly thought to have been a fish-eater that used its long teeth to catch slippery prey.
facts.quote: Dorygnathus is commonly thought to have been piscivorous, catching fish and other slippery prey with its long teeth.

facts.statement: Direct evidence of diet includes gut contents containing the teleost fish Leptolepis.
facts.quote: This is supported by direct dietary evidence based on the gut contents containing a teleost fish Leptolepis.

facts.statement: Some specimens show tooth wear consistent with eating hard food items like crustaceans and mollusks.
facts.quote: Some Dorygnathus specimens have teeth exhibiting enamel wear consistent with the consumption of hard food items (such as crustaceans and mollusks).

facts.statement: The smallest known Dorygnathus specimen has a wingspan of sixty centimetres, and no juveniles are known.
facts.quote: Very young juveniles of Dorygnathus are unknown, the smallest discovered specimen having a wingspan of sixty centimetres

facts.statement: Researcher Padian concluded that Dorygnathus grew rapidly as a juvenile and continued growing slowly after maturity, potentially reaching a wingspan of 1.7 metres.
facts.quote: Padian concluded that Dorygnathus after a relatively fast growth in its early years, faster than any modern reptile of the same size, kept slowly growing after having reached sexual maturity, which would have resulted in exceptionally large individuals with a 1.7 m wingspan.

facts.statement: Most researchers today assume that Dorygnathus moved on all fours.
facts.quote: Most researchers however, today assume quadrupedality for all pterosaurs.

facts.statement: The genus Dorygnathus was described by Wagner in 1860.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Wagner, 1860

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Dorygnathus banthensis, originally described by Theodori in 1830 and named by Wagner in 1860.
facts.quote: subdivision: Dorygnathus banthensis (Theodori, 1830) Wagner, 1860 (tipo)

facts.statement: Baron Franz Nopcsa assigned Dorygnathus to the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae in 1928, a classification confirmed by Peter Wellnhofer in 1978.
facts.quote: Baron Franz Nopcsa in 1928 assigned the species to the Rhamphorhynchinae, which was confirmed by Peter Wellnhofer in 1978.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic analyses have not reached a consensus on the exact relationships of Dorygnathus.
facts.quote: Modern exact cladistic analyses of the relationships of Dorygnathus have not resulted in a consensus.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding Dorygnathus's position, with David Unwin placing it in Rhamphorhynchinae while Alexander Kellner placed it in a more basal position.
facts.quote: David Unwin in 2003 found that it belonged to the clade Rhamphorhynchinae, but analyses by Alexander Kellner resulted in a much more basal position, below Dimorphodon or Peteinosaurus.

facts.statement: Padian suggested in 2008 that Dorygnathus formed a series of successive off-shoots rather than a separate clade with Scaphognathus and Rhamphorhynchus.
facts.quote: Padian, using a comparative method, in 2008 concluded that Dorygnathus was close to Scaphognathus and Rhamphorhynchus in the phylogenetic tree but also that these species were forming a series of successive off-shoots, meaning that they would not be united in a separate clade.

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Brian Andres contradicted Padian's view by showing Dorygnathus was part of a monophyletic Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: This was again contradicted by the results of a cladistic study by Brian Andres in 2010 showing that Dorygnathus was part of a monophyletic Rhamphorhynchinae.

facts.statement: Dorygnathus exhibited heterodonty, having different types of teeth, a condition rare in modern reptiles but common in primitive pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Tener dientes diferentes, una condición llamada heterodoncia, es raro entre los reptiles modernos pero era común entre los pterosaurios primitivos.

facts.statement: The fifth digit of Dorygnathus's hind limbs was unusually long and oriented sideways.
facts.quote: El quinto dígito de sus miembros posteriores era inusualmente largo y orientado hacia los lados.

facts.statement: The extreme length of Dorygnathus's front teeth allowed them to project beyond the head margins when the beak was closed.
facts.quote: The long upper and lower front teeth interlaced when the beak was closed; due to their extreme length they then projected considerably beyond the upper and lower margins of the head.

facts.statement: The first remains of Dorygnathus were discovered near Banz, Bavaria, and described in 1830 by Carl Theodori.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Dorygnathus, huesos aislados y fragmentos de mandíbulas encontrados en el Schwarzjura y la Caliza de Posidonia que datan del Toarciano, fueron descubiertos cerca de Banz, Baviera y fueron descritos en 1830 por Carl Theodori como Ornithocephalus banthensis

facts.statement: More complete remains of Dorygnathus have been found in German locations including Holzmaden, Ohmden, and Zell.
facts.quote: Desde entonces se han hallado restos mucho más completos en otras localidades alemanas sobre todo en Württemberg, incluyendo Holzmaden, Ohmden y Zell.

facts.statement: A specimen of Dorygnathus was excavated in Nancy, France, in 1978.
facts.quote: Un espécimen, SMNS 81840, fue excavado en 1978 en Nancy, Francia.

facts.statement: Approximately fifty specimens of Dorygnathus are currently known.
facts.quote: Hasta ahora se conocen cerca de cincuenta especímenes

facts.statement: Dorygnathus had the general constitution of a basal pterosaur, characterized by a short neck, a long tail, and short metacarpals.
facts.quote: Dorygnathus tenía la constitución general de un pterosaurio basal (es decir, un pterosaurio no pterodactiloide): un cuello corto, una cola larga y metacarpianos cortos

facts.statement: The first three pairs of teeth in the lower jaw of Dorygnathus were very long, sharp, and pointed outward and forward.
facts.quote: En la mandíbula inferior los tres primeros pares de dientes son muy alargados, afilados y apuntando hacia afuera y hacia adelante.

facts.statement: Dorygnathus possessed at least 44 teeth in total.
facts.quote: El número total de dientes es de al menos 44.

facts.statement: The humerus of Dorygnathus featured a triangular deltpectoral crest and was pneumatized.
facts.quote: El húmero tiene una cresta triangular deltopectoral y está neumatizada.

facts.statement: The lower part of the arm of Dorygnathus was 60% longer than the upper part.
facts.quote: La parte inferior del brazo es 60% más largo que la superior.

facts.statement: The first three metacarpals of Dorygnathus were connected to three small fingers equipped with short, highly curved claws.
facts.quote: Los tres primeros metacarpianos están conectados a tres pequeños dedos, equipados con garras cortas y muy curvadas

facts.statement: The ilium of Dorygnathus was elongated, with a length equivalent to six vertebrae.
facts.quote: El ilion es alargado y con una longitud equivalente a seis vértebras.

facts.statement: The lower part of the leg of adult Dorygnathus, where the lower two-thirds of the tibia and fibula are fused, was one-third shorter than the femur.
facts.quote: La parte inferior de la pata, en la cual los dos tercios inferiores de la tibia y la fíbula de los especímenes adultos se encuentran fusionados, es un tercio más corta que el fémur

facts.statement: It is unknown whether the tail of Dorygnathus possessed a diamond-shaped structure at its end, as seen in Rhamphorhynchus.
facts.quote: Se desconoce si la cola poseía una estructura en forma de diamante en su final, como ocurre en Rhamphorhynchus.

facts.statement: Ferdinand Broili reported the presence of fur on specimen BSP 1938 I 49, suggesting Dorygnathus had hair and a high metabolism.
facts.quote: Ferdinand Broili reportó la presencia de pelaje en el espécimen BSP 1938 I 49, una indicación de que Dorygnathus también tenía pelo y un elevado metabolismo, como se cree que era propio de los pterosaurios.

facts.statement: The long front teeth of both jaws of Dorygnathus interlocked when the mouth closed, projecting beyond the upper and lower edges of the head.
facts.quote: Los dientes largos de la zona frontal de ambas mandíbulas se entrelazaban cuando se cerraba la boca; debido a su gran longitud se proyectaban más allá de los bordes superiores e inferiores de la cabeza.

facts.statement: Rupert Wild described and named the second species Dorygnathus mistelgauensis in 1971.
facts.quote: En 1971 Rupert Wild describió y nombró a una segunda especie en el género: Dorygnathus mistelgauensis

facts.statement: The specimen for Dorygnathus mistelgauensis was collected from a brick quarry near the Mistelgau train station.
facts.quote: basada en un espécimen que fue recolectado en una cantera de ladrillo cerca de la estación de tren de Mistelgau

facts.statement: The fossil of Dorygnathus mistelgauensis includes a shoulder blade, wing, partial leg, rib, and tail vertebra.
facts.quote: El fósil abarca un omóplato y un ala, una pata parcial, una costilla y una vértebra caudal

facts.statement: Wild justified the new species by its larger size, with a wingspan nearly 50% larger than the type specimen of Dorygnathus.
facts.quote: Wild justificó la creación de una nueva especie por su mayor tamaño, con una envergadura que sería cerca de un 50% más grande que en el espécimen tipo de Dorygnathus

facts.statement: In 2008, Padian noted that the largest known specimen of D. banthensis, MBR 1977.21, has a wingspan of 169 centimeters.
facts.quote: Padian en 2008 señaló que el espécimen MBR 1977.21 de D. banthensis, el mayor hasta entonces conocido, tiene una envergadura de 169centímetros

facts.statement: Baron Franz Nopcsa assigned both Dorygnathus and Dimorphodon to the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae in 1928.
facts.quote: El Barón Franz Nopcsa en 1928 asignó a ambos géneros a la subfamilia Rhamphorhynchinae

facts.statement: Modern cladistic analyses of Dorygnathus relationships have not reached a consensus.
facts.quote: Los modernos y más precisos análisis cladísticos de las relaciones de Dorygnathus no han obtenido un consenso

facts.statement: David Unwin found in 2003 that Dorygnathus belonged to the clade Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: David Unwin en 2003 encontró que pertenecía al clado Rhamphorhynchinae

facts.statement: Alexander Kellner's analyses resulted in a much more basal position for Dorygnathus, below Dimorphodon or Peteinosaurus.
facts.quote: los análisis de Alexander Kellner resultaron en una posición mucho más basal, inferior a la de Dimorphodon o Peteinosaurus

facts.statement: In 2008, Padian concluded that Dorygnathus was close to Scaphognathus and Rhamphorhynchus in the phylogenetic tree.
facts.quote: Padian, usando el método comparativo en 2008 concluyó que Dorygnathus era cercano a Scaphognathus y a Rhamphorhynchus en el árbol filogenético

facts.statement: A 2010 cladistic study by Brian Andres showed that Dorygnathus was part of a monophyletic Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: Brian Andres en 2010 mostrando que Dorygnathus era parte de un Rhamphorhynchinae monofilético

facts.statement: The genus Dorygnathus was named by Wagner in 1860.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Dorygnathus (genus), Wagner 1860

facts.statement: The parent group of Dorygnathus is Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rhamphorhynchinae

facts.statement: Dorygnathus belongs to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Rhamphorhynchidae

facts.statement: Dorygnathus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Dorygnathus lived during the Toarcian age, from 184.2 to 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dorygnathus is generally considered a piscivore that caught fish and other slippery marine creatures with its long teeth.
facts.quote: Dorygnathus es por lo general considerado como un piscívoro, capturando peces y otras criaturas marinas resbaladizas con sus largos dientes

facts.statement: Fossils of Dorygnathus have been found in marine sediments deposited in the seas of the ancient European archipelago.
facts.quote: sus fósiles se han hallado en sedimentos marinos, depositados en los mares del antiguo archipiélago europeo

facts.statement: Individuals of Dorygnathus could reach an exceptional wingspan of 1.7 meters.
facts.quote: resultando en los individuos excepcionalmente grandes que llegaban a los 1.7metros de envergadura

facts.statement: On land, Dorygnathus was probably a poor climber as its claws show no special adaptations for that type of locomotion.
facts.quote: En tierra, Dorygnathus era probablemente un mal trepador; sus garras no muestran adaptaciones especiales para ese tipo de locomoción

facts.statement: According to Padian, Dorygnathus was very capable of bipedal locomotion due to being a relatively small pterosaur with a long tail.
facts.quote: De acuerdo a Padian, Dorygnathus, siendo un pterosaurio relativamente pequeño con una cola larga, era muy capaz de una locomoción bípeda

facts.statement: Most pterosaur researchers agree that all pterosaurs were quadrupeds, contrasting with Padian's view on Dorygnathus.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los investigadores de pterosaurios concuerdan que todos los pterosaurios eran cuadrúpedos
